item.title: Elder Abhaya (2): “Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost — Attending to a pleasing sign, The mind feels infatuation, Clinging to the perception remains. The…
item.description:
Elder Abhaya (2):
“Seeing a form, mindfulness is lost —
Attending to a pleasing sign,
The mind feels infatuation,
Clinging to the perception remains.
The defilements increase,
Leading to the root of existence.”

From: Theragāthā 1.98

item.title: “Mind precedes all mental states, Mind is their chief; they are all mind-made. If with an impure mind one speaks or acts, Suffering follows like…
item.description:
“Mind precedes all mental states,
Mind is their chief; they are all mind-made.
If with an impure mind one speaks or acts,
Suffering follows like the wheel that follows the ox’s foot.”

“Mind precedes all mental states,
Mind is their chief; they are all mind-made.
If with a pure mind one speaks or acts,
Happiness follows like a shadow that never leaves.”

From: Dhammapada 1-20

item.title: “Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The…
item.description:
“Monks, these five perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless. What five? The perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world. These five perceptions, monks, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, ending in the deathless.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.62
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “What is wandering without a standing place? The bondage of standing and clinging to the sign of forms, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata,…
item.description:
“What is wandering without a standing place? The bondage of standing and clinging to the sign of forms, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future. Therefore, the Tathāgata is called ‘one who wanders without a standing place.’ The bondage of standing and clinging to the sign of sounds … smells … tastes … touches … phenomena, householder, has been abandoned by the Tathāgata … Therefore, the Tathāgata is called ‘one who wanders without a standing place.’ Thus, householder, is wandering without a standing place.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.3

item.title: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain and truly knows: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected:…
item.description:
“Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain and truly knows: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will not attend to the sign of the beautiful. By not attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will not pollute his mind. He will die without greed, without ill-will, without delusion, without stain, his mind unpolluted.’”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 5 – Anaṅgaṇasutta

item.title: Four wheels, nine doors, Full of defilement, tied by greed — Mired in mud, O great hero, What will be the future state Of such…
item.description:
Four wheels, nine doors,
Full of defilement, tied by greed —
Mired in mud,
O great hero,
What will be the future state
Of such a human birth?

(The Blessed One):
Having cut off delight and bondage,
Sensual desire and evil,
Having destroyed the root of craving —
Such will be his future state.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 2.28
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “I do not see any other sound, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the sound of a woman. The…
item.description:
“I do not see any other sound, monks, that so obsesses and occupies the mind of a man as the sound of a woman. The sound of a woman, monks, obsesses and occupies the mind of a man.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 1.2

item.title: “And how, monks, is a monk ‘washed clean’? He has washed away evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful…
item.description:
“And how, monks, is a monk ‘washed clean’? He has washed away evil, unwholesome states that are defiling, leading to renewed existence, fearful, producing painful results, leading to future birth, aging, and death. Thus, monks, a monk is ‘washed clean.’”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 39 – Mahāhatthipadopamasutta

item.title: “Monks, if that monk, while examining the peril in those thoughts, still has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arising, then that…
item.description:
“Monks, if that monk, while examining the peril in those thoughts, still has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arising, then that monk should not attend to, not give attention to those thoughts. By not attending to, not giving attention to those thoughts, those evil, unwholesome thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandonment, the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated. Monks, just as a person with eyes, not wanting to see forms within his range, would close his eyes or look away; so too, monks, that monk, by not attending … the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 20 – Vitakkasaṇṭhānasutta

item.title: “Monk, whoever thinks about form is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about form is freed from the Evil One. Whoever thinks about feeling…
item.description:
“Monk, whoever thinks about form is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about form is freed from the Evil One. Whoever thinks about feeling … perception … formations … consciousness is bound by Māra. Whoever does not think about consciousness is freed from the Evil One. This brief saying of mine, monk, should be understood in detail.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.64
